bad.title: New folder looks like a place
bad.text: It sits between Photos and Trash, so people expect a page, not an action.

bad.title: Upload sends people away too
bad.text: It opens a page of its own, and the photo lands in Files, not Photos.

bad.title: The folder ends up in Files
bad.text: People started in Photos and now sit somewhere else, away from what they were doing.
bad.wait: Press New folder, then Create, to see this.

good.title: Only places in the sidebar
good.text: Files, Photos and Trash. Every item goes somewhere.

good.title: New folder acts on this page
good.text: The folder appears in Photos, where people already are.

good.title: It says where the folder went
good.text: “Summer trip” lands at the top of Photos, in plain view.
good.wait: Press New folder to see this.

bad.title: Eleven items, all the same weight
bad.text: Orders, used every day, looks no different from Staff, set up once.

bad.title: Setup pages among the daily ones
bad.text: Shipping, Taxes and Payments sit in the same list as Orders and Products.

good.title: Sell and Grow as headings
good.text: People skip to the right group instead of reading all eleven.

good.title: Rare pages fold under More (2)
good.text: Gift cards and Reviews stay one click away, out of the way.

good.title: Setup moves into Settings
good.text: Shipping, Taxes, Payments and Staff wait there, off the daily list.

bad.title: Five icons, no words
bad.text: People point at each one to read its tooltip, and do it again next time.

bad.title: Presets is just a cube
bad.text: Nothing about the shape says presets, so people hover until they hit it.

good.title: Every icon carries its name
good.text: Library, Adjust, Layers, Presets and Help, readable at a glance.

good.title: Presets, found by reading
good.text: The label does the first finding, and the cube helps people remember it.

bad.title: No item is marked
bad.text: Home, Search and Library look the same, so the sidebar can’t say where people are.

bad.title: “Your music” matches nothing
bad.text: No sidebar item uses those words, so people can’t link the page to Library.

good.title: Library is highlighted
good.text: The sidebar answers where people are at a glance.

good.title: The title says Library too
good.text: Page and sidebar use the same word, so either side confirms it.

bad.title: Home / My trips above My trips
bad.text: The trail repeats the title right under it, one more line to read.

bad.title: Stays already goes home
bad.text: The logo does the job of the trail’s Home link.

good.title: The title alone says where people are
good.text: My trips, with nothing repeated above it.

good.title: Stays still leads home
good.text: The trail’s Home link isn’t missed, because the logo covers it.

good.title: One link covers the way up
good.text: ← My trips is named for where it goes.
good.wait: Open a trip to see this.

bad.title: Search, Sale, Wishlist, in visiting order
bad.text: None of them is where running shoes live in the shop.

bad.title: Search starts the trail, not the shop
bad.text: It leads back to results for “gifts”, not to more shoes.

good.title: Shoes, then Running
good.text: The same trail however people got here, from a search, a sale or a link.

good.title: More running shoes, one click away
good.text: Running opens Road racer 2 and the GTX next to this one.

bad.title: Seven levels fill the trail
bad.text: It wraps onto a second line and pushes March and its files down.

bad.title: Clients, third of seven
bad.text: People read past Files and Work to reach it, every time.

good.title: Files / … / March on one line
good.text: The top level and the current one, with the page right below.

good.title: … holds the five middle levels
good.text: Work through Invoices stay one click away, without taking up the line.

good.title: Clients in a short list
good.text: The hidden levels appear in order, so the jump takes two clicks.

bad.title: Address and Card are ticked but locked
bad.text: They show as done, yet a click on either does nothing.

bad.title: Review lists the answers with no Edit
bad.text: Switching to Work costs Back, Back, a pick, Next and Next.

bad.title: Five clicks for one change
bad.text: That cost is why people stop checking their answers.

good.title: Finished steps open with a click
good.text: Address is one press away from Review, skipping Card.

good.title: Edit beside each answer
good.text: It opens that step, and Next becomes Back to review.

good.title: Three clicks for one change
good.text: Edit, pick Work, Back to review. Checking stays cheap.

bad.title: The same welcome every month
bad.text: Regulars read “Let’s create an invoice” before they can do anything.

bad.title: Four steps for a known invoice
bad.text: Northwind and the retainer never change, yet each gets its own screen.

bad.title: Six clicks for a repeat job
bad.text: Three Nexts, two picks and Send, every single month.

good.title: Saved templates on the first screen
good.text: Northwind · Monthly retainer is waiting, so regulars skip the questions.

good.title: Use jumps to Check and send
good.text: Client and work are filled in, and the guided path stays for newcomers.

good.title: Two clicks for a repeat job
good.text: Use, then Send invoice.

bad.title: Back clears the size
bad.text: 5×7 is no longer picked, and Next is off until people choose again.
bad.wait: Pick a size, set Copies to 3, press Next, then Back to see this.

bad.title: Copies quietly back to 1
bad.text: People who miss it order one print instead of three.
bad.wait: Set Copies to 3, press Next, then Back to see this.

good.title: The size is still picked
good.text: 5×7 stays pressed, so checking the step costs nothing.
good.wait: Pick a size, set Copies to 3, press Next, then Back to see this.

good.title: Copies still says 3
good.text: The number people typed survives Back, so the order stays right.
good.wait: Set Copies to 3, press Next, then Back to see this.

bad.title: Nine dots and no names
bad.text: People can count the screens but can’t tell what’s left.

bad.title: Step 1 of 9 for one flight
bad.text: Seat, bags, meals, insurance and extras each take a whole screen.

bad.title: Eight presses of Next before Pay
bad.text: Most of those screens only confirm a default that was already fine.

good.title: Three named steps on one line
good.text: Flight, Travelers, Pay. The end is in sight from the start.

good.title: Defaults in one line, with Change
good.text: Standard seat, 1 cabin bag and No meal, all changed in one place.

good.title: Two presses of Next before Pay
good.text: The seat, bags and meal no longer cost a screen each.
